collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — NATURE, ECOLOGY AND ANIMALS (NAT-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Isola's animals, plants, tides and weather: tide pools and nesting beaches, washed-up rubbish, shrinking clam beds, strange visitors, creatures doing what creatures do, and choices about the island where nobody gets a perfect answer.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: An elder sees a red-throated bird thought gone for years: tell the whole village, or keep the place secret.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) comes back from the high forest out of breath and shaking with excitement. (subject.He/she) saw a little bird with a curved beak and a bright red throat. There used to be lots of them, when (subject.he/she) was a child. Nobody has seen one in so long that most people thought they were gone forever. (friend) is the first person (subject) finds to tell.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The news spreads by lunchtime. By the afternoon, a crowd of hopeful villagers is tramping through the high forest, whispering loudly. Nobody sees the bird. Some of them are fairly sure (subject) saw a different bird. (subject) is certain. (friend) believes (subject.him/her). One bird is not a flock, (friend) says, and it might be the very last one. But it might not.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "If there's one, there might be a nest," (friend) says quietly. "And if there's a nest, it doesn't need forty people stamping around it." (subject) agrees. The two of them go back alone, every few days, and sit very still. On the fifth visit, they hear it: a thin, high little song from deep in the leaves. They never do find out if there are any more. They keep going back anyway.
